root_cause: Commit f27721f (authored by Copilot, co-authored by Claude Opus 4.6) rewrote the OBJ/MTL parser from line-based (safeGetline with null-terminated strings) to byte-stream-based StreamReader with raw buffer pointers. This changed the safety contract: tryParseDouble's internal boundary-check gaps (reading *curr before re-checking end_not_reached) became exploitable with non-null-terminated buffers. Deep verifier incorrectly concluded UNLIKELY by focusing narrowly on tryParseDouble itself, missing that the AI rewrite changed the calling context that made the existing gaps exploitable. OSS-Fuzz bisection authoritatively confirms f27721f as the introducing commit.

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: Deep verifier should consider calling-context changes that alter safety invariants, not just the vulnerable function itself
improvement_suggestions.rationale: Verifier missed that changing from null-terminated strings to raw pointers invalidated existing boundary-check assumptions in called functions

improvement_suggestions.suggestion: OSV introduced commits should be treated as strong evidence for causality attribution
improvement_suggestions.rationale: OSS-Fuzz bisection is highly reliable — verifier should not easily override it
